decisions.statement: The pages written are the pages of that page type and of every page type beneath it.
A page whose values are already in order is passed over.
A page type no page of which holds the key out of order is refused.
A count handed in holds how many pages one run carries values on.
A run handed no count carries values on every page holding the key out of order.
One page refused refuses the whole change.
A refusal names the page that drew the refusal.
Putting the values in order is left to the mechanical change acting on a page type.
That change is reached through the runner rather than by an import.
Nothing here works out a body of its own.
Nothing here reads a page's own body.
A key holding no list is passed over rather than refused.

definition: the values one key holds carried into the order they sort in, on every page of one page type
